design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one ordinary thing — take the deposit that falls due this week — and the figure she must be given cannot be reached without doing the desk's real work first. The deposit is a share of the room rate standing on the folio, and this reservation's folio carries no room rate at all: two payments and nothing else. So the agent must read the deposit terms, see what the figure waits on, look at the folio, find it empty of room rate, work out from the pricing terms what the stay is worth, post it, and only then work the deposit out on the world that leaves behind. Both figures are multi-factor: the room rate turns on the window mix of a stay that straddles the close of the peak window, a pass registered to the lead guest, how far ahead the booking was made, the length of the stay, the household's other holdings and the make-up of the party; the deposit turns on which window the arrival falls in, a protection plan written over this very reservation, the household's dining and hire holdings and the money already collected on this folio as against money collected on a different stay. Nothing is guessable from the tool list: both tools take a number and write it, and both would write a wrong number just as happily. The stay is deliberately one where the record's own rate window field and the window the nights are actually priced in part company, so an agent who prices the stay off the field reaches neither gold nor the computation document's fall-back.

SCOPE (Principle C). Already occupied before this task: nothing, this is task 0 of 2. Claimed here: lodging_ext_stay_rate_posting (subject lodging_room_charge, tool post_stay_room_charge_ee3504ba) and lodging_ext_reservation_deposit (subject lodging_deposit_charge, tool authorise_reservation_deposit_3e63cb2f) — the pricing of a booked stay onto its folio and the deposit asked for before arrival. Left free for task 1, whose draw is three prerequisite problems: everything on the far side of the stay — the resort charge posted for nights occupied, the fee posted when nights are given up, the departure services charge, the settlement collected at the end. Task 1 therefore has an independent load-bearing space of four problems on a stay that is over, with its own tools, and it is not forced to re-use either policy or either tool claimed here.

STEP 0 DRAW, as printed by scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/tasks/lodging_reservations_desk --task 0:
{"task": 0, "key": "ski_resort_operator/lodging_reservations_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4]}
The tree is therefore the root plus exactly one prerequisite problem, and the two computations carry 6 and 4 declared factors. The room rate posting took the 6 and the deposit took the 4; the multiset matches the draw.

POLICIES CLAIMED, LINEAGE AND TRIGGER.
lodging_ext_stay_rate_posting: base_policy_refs [lodging_agg_household_stay_pricing, lodging_rate_and_fees] — the two base policies whose subject includes lodging_room_charge. trigger state_due: with no customer calling at all, a booked stay that has not been priced onto its folio is money the collective should have on its books, so month-end reconciliation would want it. Six clauses of base are superseded, each named verbatim in overwrite: the posting grain (night by night as one figure per night) becomes one entry covering the stay; the night-by-night window reading is replaced for a straddling stay by the window-mix rule; the three reduction sentences are replaced by the three ladders; and base's flat extra person charge ("Guests beyond the unit type's standard occupancy add the extra person charge to each night they stay.") is replaced by the family-share sentence of the occupancy ladder. What remains inherited untouched is everything those six sentences do not name: that reductions are worked out in a fixed order and frozen on the reservation, that reservations sharing dates are priced on their own and nights are never pooled, that the resort charge is not reduced by any discount, that a night the party leaves early is still charged, that the housekeeping charge is posted once on departure and the parking charge nightly, and the whole of the occupancy and dedup machinery of lodging_agg_multi_holding.
lodging_ext_reservation_deposit: base_policy_refs [lodging_deposit_terms, lodging_rate_and_fees, lodging_stay_operations]; only the first governs the subject lodging_deposit_charge, and lodging_rate_and_fees is input lineage for the nightly resort charge the holiday tier reads. lodging_stay_operations is not mere lineage: this policy collects the incidental hold in advance, where base takes it at check-in, so base's sentence "The incidental hold is taken at check-in against the lead guest's own payment method and is not taken against a third party's card." is named verbatim in overwrite and replaced by the sentence that collects it with the deposit. trigger state_due: a reservation standing with a deposit due date in front of it and nothing held against it owes that deposit whether or not the household rings. The second declared override names base's deposit sentence and replaces it with the working-base sentence. The deposit period, the counting rule, the states in which a deposit may be taken, the release of a hold whose deposit does not clear and the balance falling due before arrival are all inherited untouched, and the first two are carried into solvability_contract as base preconditions.

FACTOR CARD — lodging_ext_stay_rate_posting (6 declared), gold 4062.89.
1 passholder_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty on passes, multi-source): tiers are a pass standing active for the season registered to the lead guest / a pass standing active for the season registered to someone else / no active pass. Tier taken: the first, on passes_holdings PA1 (active, 2026-27, Karin Ostergaard) read against lodging_holdings.lead_guest_name. Baseline: no passholder reduction; result 4733.28. Near-miss: PA2, a Midweek pass for the same season in Tomas Ostergaard's name, standing cancelled.
2 advance_booking_reduction (parameter, date span): twice the advance period / the advance period / less. Tier taken: the middle, 2026-12-01 to 2027-03-12 is 101 days against the unit type's 90. Baseline: none; 4733.28. Near-miss: the deposit due date 2026-12-06 sits between the two dates and is the wrong anchor.
3 length_of_stay_reduction (parameter, date span): twice the threshold / the threshold / fewer. Tier taken: the middle, eight nights against a threshold of 7. Baseline: none; 4484.99.
4 package_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty on lessons, multi-source): both a confirmed school booking and a confirmed rental agreement / either one / neither. Tier taken: the middle, on lessons_holdings LS1 (confirmed) with rentals_holdings RN1 standing cancelled. Baseline: none; 4160.30. Near-misses: LS2, a cancelled Mountain Cubs booking, and RN1 itself.
5 straddling_window_pricing (method): more than half the nights in the higher window / half or fewer / no straddle. Tier taken: the second, three of eight nights inside the peak window that closes 2027-03-14 and five outside it, so every night is priced at the lower window's base nightly rate of 749.00 for 5992.00. Baseline (the computation document's standard method, each night on its own window): 3 x 1050.00 + 5 x 749.00 = 6895.00, giving 4635.39.
6 occupancy_charge_rate (parameter, party record and date span): larger than standard occupancy with children / larger, adults only, filling the unit / every other case. Tier taken: the first, three adults and two children against a standard occupancy of 4 and a maximum of 6. Baseline: the unit type's own 55.00 a night; 4238.89.
Whole-baseline fall-back (every factor at its fall-through, the figure an agent gets from the computation document alone): 7335.00, against gold 4062.89.

FACTOR CARD — lodging_ext_reservation_deposit (4 declared), gold 867.29.
1 deposit_working_base (method): arrival inside the holiday window (room rate plus the nightly resort charge for every night) / arrival inside the peak window (the whole room rate standing on the folio) / otherwise (the nightly average times the fewest nights the unit type is let for outside both windows). Tier taken: the middle, arrival 2027-03-12. Baseline: 250.00.
2 protected_deposit_share (parameter, cross-difficulty on insure, multi-source): a plan standing active over the reservation whose remaining benefit reaches the room rate / falls short of it / no plan. Tier taken: the middle, insure_holdings IN1 active over this lodging_id with benefit_remaining_usd 3600.00 against a room rate of 4062.89. Baseline: the unit type's 35 per cent; 1172.01. Near-miss: the same plan's covered_value_usd of 5200.00 does reach the room rate, and reading that field instead of the benefit moves the share to 20 per cent.
3 incidental_prepay_share (parameter, cross-difficulty on dining, multi-source): both a dining plan standing active and a rental agreement standing confirmed / either / neither. Tier taken: the middle, dining_holdings DN1 active with no confirmed rental. Baseline: the whole 500.00 hold; 1117.29.
4 payments_already_collected (parameter, folio history): payments reaching the share / one or more payments short of it / no payment at all. Tier taken: the middle, 300.00 + 200.00 = 500.00 against a share of 1117.29475. Baseline: nothing taken off; 1367.29. Near-miss: the 1212.00 payment on the closed 2025-26 stay, which an account-wide sum sweeps in.
Whole-baseline fall-back: 855.50, against gold 867.29.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. The two gold writes have two exact subjects.
Subject lodging_room_charge is governed by lodging_agg_household_stay_pricing and lodging_rate_and_fees. Neither carries an eligibility gate that applies to a room charge: the only structured gate in either, resort_fee_stay_state, binds the posting of a resort charge. Both therefore enter solvability_contract as policy_scope, with their scope stated. There is no time gate on this write, so no anchor question arises.
Subject lodging_deposit_charge is governed by lodging_deposit_terms alone, and both of its gates apply.
  deposit_due_period (kind time): condition verbatim "The deposit is taken no later than the unit type's deposit period counted in calendar days from the day the unit was put on hold." Starting business event: the unit was put on hold. Authoritative anchor: lodging_holdings.booked_date = 2026-12-01 (never the deposit_due_date field, which is a convenience the collective wrote down). Clock: frozen_time 2026-12-04. Duration source: variants.deposit_due_days, 5 for a Mountain Lodge Suite. Counting rule copied verbatim from base: calendar days counted forward, the anchor date itself day zero, every day of the week alike, never mixed with 24-hour periods. Direction: not_after. Boundary: inclusive. Positive case: at frozen_time the count stands at 3 of 5, inside the boundary; at 2026-12-06, day five exactly, the deposit may still be taken. Negative case: on 2026-12-07 the period has run out and the correct handling is that the hold is released and the household told, not that a deposit is taken.
  deposit_chargeable_state (kind state): condition verbatim "A deposit is taken only while the reservation stands in the held, deposit_pending or confirmed state." The reservation stands deposit_pending at frozen_time and is not moved by either gold write, so it is in the allowed set at the moment of the write. Evidence is the official row, never the caller: she says only that a note told her the sixth.
Both gates correlate to the action by lodging_holdings.lodging_id, which is exactly the parameter the deposit tool takes.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The object is one reservation: the Mountain Lodge Suite at Silverpine Basin for 2027-03-12 to 2027-03-20, lodging_holdings row b41d7e60-2c58-4a3e-9f27-6d0a83c15e9b. The correlation key is lodging_id, and every folio entry carries it. Rows included in the deposit arithmetic: the two payments on that reservation, 300.00 and 200.00, and the room rate entry this call posts to it. Rows excluded and why: the five folio entries of the closed 2025-26 Slopeside Studio stay carry a different lodging_id, so the 1116.00 room rate on that folio is not the room rate standing on this one and the 1212.00 payment is not a payment against this stay. Nothing has been reversed, compensated or adjusted on either reservation: the closed stay's deposit of 279.00 was returned, answering to the deposit entry it came from through related_event_id, and that is the only derived row in the seed. The tool writes the reservation reference onto every row it creates, so the new room rate entry and the new deposit entry are both correlated to the source object rather than to the account.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS, AND WHAT CHANGES IF IT GOES.
customers 8f2b...b204: the account the call is about; remove it and the call cannot start. Its mobile number is the locator and its date of birth and postal code are the two details the verification threshold needs.
lodging_holdings b41d...5e9b: the reservation itself. Its variant fixes every tier parameter, its dates fix the window mix and the lead time, its party fixes the occupancy charge, its status and deposit due date are the two base gates, and its folio balance of -500.00 is the visible fact that no room rate has been posted. Its rate_plan field records the peak window its arrival night falls in; the nights are priced in the base window, so the field is evidence of the arrival window and never of the outcome (see the stamp note below).
lodging_holdings e0c9...d310 with its five folio entries: a completed stay from last season. It is the account history a real household carries, and it is the near-miss: its 1116.00 room rate and its 1212.00 payment both sit in the same tables as the figures this task needs, and only the reservation reference tells them apart.
lodging_folio 2a6f...f501 and 5c18...8d6a: the two payments already collected against the March stay. Remove either and the deposit changes: the amount taken off falls to 200.00 or 300.00.
passes_holdings PA1: the active pass registered to the lead guest; remove it and the passholder reduction goes and the room rate rises to 4733.28. PA2: the cancelled pass in another name, the near-miss.
lessons_holdings LS1: the confirmed school booking that puts the household on the half package tier; remove it and the room rate rises to 4160.30. LS2: the cancelled booking, a near-miss for the same factor.
rentals_holdings RN1: a cancelled hire, load-bearing as a negative on two factors at once — the package reduction stays at half rather than full, and the incidental prepay stays at half rather than nothing.
insure_holdings IN1: the protection plan written over this very reservation; remove it and the deposit share reverts to the unit type's 35 per cent and the deposit rises to 1172.01. Its covered value of 5200.00 against its remaining benefit of 3600.00 is the near-miss inside the row.
dining_holdings DN1: the active dining plan; remove it and the incidental prepay doubles to the whole 500.00 hold.
Automatic clauses checked before seeding: the deposit period (running, three days used of five, not expired); the release of a hold whose deposit has not cleared (not yet due, so nothing is owed to the household); the balance falling due the unit type's balance period before arrival (21 days before 2027-03-12 is 2027-02-19, far beyond frozen_time, so no balance obligation is lit); the closed stay's closure condition (both balances zero). No seeded row lights an obligation this task set does not carry. No cache field is in play: folio_balance_usd agrees exactly with the entries beneath it (-500.00 = -300.00 - 200.00) and deposit_held_usd with its own (0.00).

THE STAMP, AND WHY READING IT IS NOT READING THE RULE. lodging_holdings.rate_plan is defined by the schema as the window the arrival night falls in. On this stay the arrival night, 2027-03-12, is inside the peak window, so the field reads peak; but three of the eight nights fall in that window and five outside it, so the window-mix rule prices every night at the lower window's base rate. A solver who prices the stay off the field reaches 8 x 1050.00 = 8400.00 before reductions; a solver who applies the rule reaches 5992.00; a solver who reads neither and prices night by night reaches 6895.00. Three different scored figures, so the field and the ladder are told apart by the score, and the field is what the schema says it is rather than a stamp of the factor's outcome. Gold's rate_plan argument on the folio entry is base — the window the nights were priced in — which is a fourth observable difference from the record's own field.

PERSONA DESIGN. Karin is written as a brisk professional with the collective's email in front of her; the voice carries the impatience of someone doing an errand between meetings, and the conditional behaviour is woven into the narration rather than listed. Volunteered at the opening: the surface goal (the deposit on the March suite is due this week, the note says the sixth — both facts supported by lodging_holdings.deposit_due_date) and the mobile number. Given only when asked: date of birth, postal code, email, passholder number, who the room is for, who is travelling (three adults and two children, in the record's own words), and the household's other bookings. She cannot state any figure on the account and says so. Reacted to only after the agent speaks: the payment route comes up when payment does; she runs the authorisation only once the agent has told her the amount and handed it over; she closes once she hears the deposit has gone through. Two natural traps: she says the ski hire "was cancelled weeks ago", which is true of the record and is exactly the row a careless agent counts; and she mentions the dining plan and the lesson in the same breath as the cancelled hire, so the agent must read each one's state rather than the sentence. She never names the room rate, the folio, or anything to do first, and she does not correct a wrong figure: an agent who hands her the baseline 855.50 hears the same thanks as one who hands her 867.29.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root problem: lodging_ext_reservation_deposit, the deposit the caller rang about. One prerequisite problem, matching the draw: lodging_ext_stay_rate_posting.
Edge lodging_ext_reservation_deposit <- lodging_ext_stay_rate_posting. kind value_input; gate posted_room_rate, a compute binding of the deposit policy. form state. Prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the deposit policy's own rule: "The deposit asked for is fixed only after the folio carries the room rate posted for every night of the stay." Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result, the deposit asked for, to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state — a room rate entry standing on the folio covering the nights of the stay — named in the words the folio and its finder use, with no action, performer or tool in it; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token and no row id; (4) it is written at exactly the strength of the edge, a hard "only after" over the whole stay's nights, no wider and no narrower than the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the room rate posting is the only policy in the charter whose result is a room rate entry on a folio, so a reader who finds the folio empty of room rate has one and only one place to go. Derivation: the sentence says the deposit waits on a room rate standing on the folio; the folio read shows two payments and nothing else; the pricing policy's own rule says what the room rate for a stay is and that it is posted to the folio as one entry covering every night — so the action to take first is to price the stay onto the folio, and then work the deposit out. condition: the folio of the reservation carries a room rate entry covering every night of the stay. resolved_by: post_stay_room_charge_ee3504ba, owner agent. The customer's own write in this tree is the root itself, authorise_reservation_deposit_3e63cb2f, owner user: the household's own money leaves their own card on their own instruction, which the desk may prepare but not do for them, and it completes on the spot inside the call.
Seed evidence that the edge is unmet at frozen_time: lodging_holdings.b41d...5e9b.folio_balance_usd = -500.0 with the only two folio entries on that reservation standing as lodging_payment rows of 300.00 and 200.00. Topological order: lodging_ext_stay_rate_posting, then lodging_ext_reservation_deposit. Parallel edges: none — a chain of two, so no ordering ambiguity can arise. Deletion sensitivity, recomputed by the harness rather than asserted: skipping the room rate posting leaves the deposit at 250.00 instead of 867.29 and the folio at -500.00 instead of 3562.89. The figure in prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing is that recomputation, and it agrees with the deposit_working_base sensitivity entry, which reaches the same skipped-world arithmetic. user_scenario mentions no prerequisite (see prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint), and neither tool validates one (see tools_do_not_block).

LENGTH AND BREADTH. Depth: surface goal (take the deposit) -> the deposit terms say the figure waits on a room rate standing on the folio -> the folio carries none -> the pricing terms say what the stay is worth and how it is posted -> post it -> work the deposit out on the world that leaves. Two hops, and they cannot be swapped: the deposit computed first is computed on an empty folio. Breadth, at the room rate: the window mix of the stay, the pass register, the lead time, the length of the stay, two other product lines, and the party record, each read from a different place. Breadth, at the deposit: which window the arrival falls in, a protection plan in a fourth product line, a dining plan in a fifth, and the folio's own payment history sifted by reservation. Remove any one of those and a figure moves, as the factor sensitivities show.

WHERE A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT. Pricing the eight nights night-by-night (6895.00 rather than 5992.00) — excluded by the window-mix sentence. Pricing them on the rate window the reservation record names (8400.00) — excluded because that field records the window the arrival night falls in while the rule prices the stay on the mix of its nights. Counting the lead time from the deposit due date rather than the date the reservation was recorded — excluded because the rule names the reservation being recorded. Counting the cancelled hire or the cancelled lesson as held — excluded because every tier names the state the holding stands in. Reading the protection plan's covered value instead of its remaining benefit — excluded because the tier names the benefit remaining. Summing every payment on the account (1712.00) instead of the payments against this stay (500.00) — excluded because the tier says "against the stay", and every folio entry carries the reservation it belongs to. Taking the deposit on the empty folio — excluded by the prerequisite sentence.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate the household by the mobile number; verify with two details. Read the reservations: one live, one closed. Read the folio entries for the account and sort them by reservation: this stay has two payments, 500.00, and no room rate. Read the passes, the school bookings, the hire agreements, the protection plans and the dining plans, in each case reading the state and the season rather than the existence. Work the room rate out: 8 nights, 3 of them inside the peak window and 5 outside it, so half or fewer fall in the higher window and every night is priced at the base rate: 8 x 749.00 = 5992.00; less 15 per cent passholder = 5093.20; less 15 per cent advance = 4329.22; less 10 per cent length of stay = 3896.298; less 2.5 per cent half package = 3798.89055; plus one extra guest at the family rate 33.00 for 8 nights = 264.00; rounded once = 4062.89. Post it over 8 nights on the base window. Then the deposit: arrival inside the peak window so the base is the whole 4062.89; the plan's remaining benefit 3600.00 falls short of it so the share is 27.5 per cent = 1117.29475; plus half the 500.00 hold = 250.00; less the 500.00 already collected against this stay; rounded once = 867.29. Hand the authorisation to the caller with that figure and the reservation reference; she runs it against the card on file.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The task is built by a script that evaluates each policy's compute with the gate's own evaluator (skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py: build_env, eval_compute, substitute) on the handling-time world — initial_state with every earlier gold write replayed through the real tools — so the declared expected values, the per-factor baseline results, the whole-baseline results and the skipped-edge counterfactual are the machine's output rather than the author's arithmetic. Its printed output: B 4062.89 baseline 7335.0 | A 867.29 baseline 855.5, with per-factor baselines passholder 4733.28, advance 4733.28, length-of-stay 4484.99, package 4160.30, straddling window 4635.39, occupancy rate 4238.89, working base 250.00, protected share 1172.01, incidental prepay 1117.29, payments collected 1367.29, and the skipped-edge deposit 250.00 with a folio of -500.00. The gate block then re-derives all of it independently; its output lines are recorded with the task's closing.

CLOSURE. policy -> tool -> computation -> GT call -> terminal state: lodging_ext_stay_rate_posting computes room_charge_amount_usd, the argument of post_stay_room_charge_ee3504ba at the first call, which leaves a room rate entry of 4062.89 over 8 nights on the base window and a folio balance of 3562.89; lodging_ext_reservation_deposit computes deposit_amount_usd, the argument of authorise_reservation_deposit_3e63cb2f at the second call, which leaves a deposit entry of 867.29 and a deposit of 867.29 standing against the reservation. charter_scope, required_documents and computations.policy_id name exactly those two policies; charter_scope.task_tools names exactly those two tools in first-call order; the write order is the topological order of the tree. No third write, no idle policy, no obligation left open: the balance of the stay falls due in February 2027 and is not owed now, and the reservation is not moved out of deposit_pending because the deposit clearing, not the deposit being taken, is what makes a reservation firm.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked, and only the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, the DB the finders return and the caller's own lines in hand: the caller wants the deposit taken; the deposit terms say the figure is fixed only after the folio carries the room rate posted for every night of the stay; the folio finder returns two payments and no room rate; the pricing terms state the standard method and, in their own documents, the window-mix, passholder, advance, length-of-stay, package and occupancy rules; applying them to the reservation record gives 4062.89 and the tool takes exactly that with 8 nights on the base window; the deposit terms then give 867.29 on the card the caller names. The redraft reaches the same two writes, in the same order, with the same arguments, and no second reading of any sentence produced a different figure.

MANUAL VALUES GATES, COMPLETED AFTER THE SCRIPTS PASSED.
Length, breadth and the hidden test: the two hops were walked from the surface goal to the deposit figure and are set out above; removing the room rate posting moves the scored deposit from 867.29 to 250.00 and removing any one of the ten declared factors moves one of the two figures, as the sensitivity runs show. The customer's own write is the deposit itself: the household's money leaves their own card on their own instruction, which the desk may prepare but may not do for them, and it lands inside the call.
Expression of the need and the simulator's boundary: the caller names the object (the March suite booking), the timing (the deposit due this week), the authorisation (the desk may prepare, she pays herself) and the mode (a write, not a quote). She never reads policy, never pushes the order of work, never corrects a figure and runs the authorisation only after the agent has unlocked and handed it over.
Chronology of the opening world: every fact she volunteers — the booking, the deposit falling due on the sixth, the mobile number — points at initial_state rows. Nothing she says anticipates a charge only gold creates.
Base eligibility and the time anchor: checked verbatim against lodging_deposit_terms; the anchor, the duration, the counting rule, the direction, the boundary and the two adjacent cases are set out in the base-invariant card above.
Authoritative facts and the business object: the pass register, the school booking, the hire agreement, the protection plan and the dining plan are all read from the records and never from the caller's summary of them; every folio row entering an aggregate carries the March reservation's own reference, and the five rows of the closed 2025-26 stay are excluded by that same key.
Reachability and no real-world waits: every figure is computable from records already held, both writes land synchronously under one frozen_time, and nothing waits on a diagnosis, a delivery, a clearing, a review or a future date. Each must-ask question has a definite answer in the persona, including the one she cannot answer.
Prerequisite sentence: the four-point test is set out in the problem-tree card, the state form was available and used, exactly one write of this difficulty brings the state about, and the rule carries nothing else about the dependency.
Two-way equivalence of rule and compute: every binding quotes a rule sentence verbatim (checked mechanically over compute_basis), every ladder is stated in the rule tier by tier with its condition and its value or method, and no tier states which tier this customer is on. The reverse sweep found no rule sentence carrying a quantity, window, filter, branch, cap or rounding semantic that no binding implements.
Factors bear weight, the labels are honest, the baseline is honest: each factor's baseline is exactly what the policy's baseline paragraph states for that input; the two method factors change how a quantity is computed rather than swapping a number; the eight parameter factors select values the charter states; no two tiers of any ladder share an outcome, and the payments ladder's middle tier now reads "one or more payments", so its third tier is the only tier a folio with no payment reaches; the near-miss records are present and excluded by the rule alone; and the whole-baseline figures, 7335.00 and 855.50, are both definite and both different from gold.
Draft recomputation from the visible context: performed and recorded above; it reached the same two writes in the same order with the same arguments.

AUDIT RESPONSE — round 3, against env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/audits/policy_task/lodging_reservations_desk/0.md and _difficulty.md. Each item is answered by its own id.
T0-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, a tier read off a stamp). Closed by making the field and the rule disagree. The stay now runs 2027-03-12 to 2027-03-20, eight nights, three of them inside the peak window and five outside it, so the window-mix ladder takes its second tier and prices every night at the lower window's base rate. The reservation's rate_plan field still reads peak, which is what the schema says it holds — the window the arrival night falls in — but the nights are priced in the base window, so a solver reading the field reaches 8400.00 before reductions, a solver applying the ladder reaches 5992.00, and a solver reading neither reaches 6895.00: three different scored figures, told apart by the score. Gold's rate_plan argument on the folio entry is base, a fourth observable difference. user_scenario:
Karin Ostergaard is a landscape architect in Boulder who has skied Silverpine Basin since her twenties and now takes her two children and her sister's family up there every March. She is brisk on the phone, a little impatient with hold music, and she has the collective's email open in front of her while she talks. She opens with the plain version of what she wants: the deposit on the suite they have booked for March is due this week, the note says the sixth, and she would rather get it out of the way this morning than have the hold quietly fall over while she is on site somewhere. She calls from the mobile the collective has for her, 3035550417, and gives that number first if the agent asks how to find the account.

She will not read out anything else about herself until she is asked for it, and then only the piece asked for: her date of birth is 1979-04-22, her home postal code is 80302, her email is karin.ostergaard@northpeakmail.com, and the passholder number on her media is GR44017382. If the agent asks her to confirm who the room is booked for she says it is in her own name, and if asked who is travelling she says three adults and two children, which is what she told them when she booked. She does not know and will not guess at any figure on the account: asked what she thinks is owed, she says that is exactly why she is calling and the desk should read it off the record.

Only if the agent asks whether the household has anything else booked around those dates does she mention that her daughter is in a ski school group that week, that they took a dining plan in the autumn, and that the ski hire her husband reserved was cancelled weeks ago because he is not coming now. She volunteers none of that otherwise, and she has no idea whether any of it matters.

She wants the money taken from the card the collective already keeps for her rather than reading a new one out over the phone, and she says so as soon as payment comes up. She is content for the desk to do whatever preparation on the booking it needs to do without narrating it to her, but the payment itself she wants to make herself: when the agent tells her the amount and hands the authorisation over to her, she runs it, using the reservation reference the agent gives her and the figure the agent states, and she takes the money from the card on file. If the agent states an amount she simply accepts it, because she has nothing of her own to compare it against, and she does not query it.

Once she hears the deposit has gone through and the booking is safe, she thanks the agent, says she will see them in March, and rings off. If the agent tells her something cannot be done or needs someone else, she does not argue; she asks what happens next and leaves it there.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: Calendar days are counted forward from the anchor date, the anchor date itself counting as day zero, every day of the week counting alike, and a calendar day is never mixed with a full 24-hour period; where the resulting boundary falls on a date that does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used.

boundary_check.just_before: Had the call come on 2026-12-07, one calendar day past the boundary, the deposit period counted forward from the anchor date 2026-12-01 as day zero would have run out on 2026-12-06 and the hold would have been released instead of a deposit being taken; the desk would be telling the household the unit had gone back into the window rather than collecting.
boundary_check.at_boundary: On 2026-12-06 itself, the fifth calendar day counted forward from 2026-12-01 with the anchor date counting as day zero, the boundary is inclusive and a deposit may still be taken; at frozen_time 2026-12-04 the count stands at three days, two clear days inside the boundary.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.room_charge_amount_usd: 4062.89. The stay runs 2027-03-12 to 2027-03-20, eight nights: three of them (12, 13 and 14 March) fall inside the unit type's published peak window, which closes on 2027-03-14, and five fall outside it in the base window, so the stay straddles two windows and half or fewer of its nights fall in the higher priced one, which prices every one of the eight nights at the Mountain Lodge Suite base nightly rate of 749.00 for 5992.00 before reductions — not the 6895.00 a night-by-night reading gives, and not the 8400.00 a reader gets who prices the stay on the peak window the reservation record names. A season pass stands active for 2026-27 registered to Karin Ostergaard, who is the lead guest named on the reservation, so the whole of the unit type's passholder reduction of 15 per cent applies and leaves 5093.20. The reservation was recorded 2026-12-01 for an arrival of 2027-03-12, 101 calendar days ahead, which is at least the unit type's advance period of 90 days but less than twice it, so the unit type's advance booking reduction of 15 per cent applies and leaves 4329.22. The stay runs eight nights, which reaches the unit type's length-of-stay threshold of 7 but not twice it, so the unit type's length-of-stay reduction of 10 per cent applies and leaves 3896.298. The household holds a school booking standing confirmed for 2026-27 but its only rental agreement for that season stands cancelled, so one of the two holdings is held and the half package reduction of 2.5 per cent applies, leaving 3798.89055. The party of three adults and two children is one guest beyond the unit type's standard occupancy of four and carries children as well as adults, so that guest is charged at the family share, 60 per cent of the 55.00 extra person nightly charge, that is 33.00 for each of the eight nights, 264.00, added after the reductions. Rounded once at the end: 4062.89.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.nights_covered: 8. The basis is the reservation record itself, which carries nights_booked 8 for an arrival of 2027-03-12 and a departure of 2027-03-20, and the policy sentence 'The room rate for a stay is worked out night by night and posted to the folio as a single entry covering every night of the stay.' Any correct agent counts the nights from the arrival date through the night before departure and reaches the same eight; no other number of nights is on the record.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.rate_plan: base. The tool's schema fixes the closed set: holiday where the nights of the entry are priced at the unit type's holiday nightly rate, peak where they are priced at its peak nightly rate, base where they are priced at its base nightly rate, and none for entries that are not room rate entries. The policy sentence 'Where half or fewer of the nights of the stay fall inside the higher priced of the two windows it straddles, every night of the stay is priced at the lower window's nightly rate.' settles which of them applies: three of the eight nights fall in the peak window and five outside it, so every night of this stay is priced at the base nightly rate and base holds. peak does not, even though the reservation record's own rate window field says peak: that field records the window the arrival night falls in, while this entry records the window the nights were priced in, and the two part company on a stay priced under that sentence. holiday does not: no night of the stay falls in the published holiday window, which closed on 2027-01-02. none does not: this entry is a room rate entry.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_method: card_on_file. The tool's schema fixes the closed set: card_on_file for the card already registered with the collective, card_at_desk for a card presented in person, bank_transfer for money sent from the household's bank, lodging_credit for lodging credit the household already holds, travel_partner where a partner settles for them, and none for entries that move no money. The caller states it herself: 'She wants the money taken from the card the collective already keeps for her rather than reading a new one out over the phone'. card_at_desk does not hold, the caller is on the telephone; bank_transfer does not, she sends nothing; lodging_credit does not, the account holds none; travel_partner does not, the booking was recorded on the account itself; none does not, the entry moves money.

edges.condition: The folio of the reservation carries a room rate entry covering every night of the stay.
edges.policy_source: The deposit asked for is fixed only after the folio carries the room rate posted for every night of the stay.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the folio of the March reservation carries no room rate at all. Its only two entries are payments, 300.00 and 200.00, and the reservation's folio balance stands at -500.00, which is the sum of those two payments with nothing charged against them; a folio on which a room rate had been posted could not stand at a negative balance of exactly the payments taken. So the room rate standing on the folio, which the deposit share is worked out on, is nothing, and a deposit worked out now would be worked out on nothing.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the room rate for the stay is posted, the folio carries a room rate entry of 4062.89 covering eight nights and the reservation's folio balance becomes 3562.89; the room rate standing on the folio takes that amount instead of nothing, and the deposit share is worked out on it.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain of two problems with one edge, so there is no pair of prerequisites that could be taken in either order: the room rate must stand on the folio before the deposit is worked out, and nothing else is waiting. Reversing the two is not an alternative order but a different answer, since the deposit worked out before the room rate is posted is worked out on an empty folio.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the room rate posting and replaying the rest unchanged, recomputed rather than asserted: the room rate standing on the folio is 0.00, the working base of the deposit is 0.00 and the deposit share is 0.00, so the payments already collected meet the whole of that share and nothing of them is taken off beyond it, leaving the incidental prepay alone; the deposit asked for falls from 867.29 to 250.0. The folio also ends without the 4062.89 room rate entry, at -500.0 instead of 3562.89.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller asks for one thing only, the deposit on the March suite: 'the deposit on the suite they have booked for March is due this week'. Nowhere does user_scenario mention the room rate, the folio, a charge that has not been posted, or anything that must be sorted out first; she explicitly cannot say what is owed ('asked what she thinks is owed, she says that is exactly why she is calling and the desk should read it off the record') and she is content for the desk to do whatever preparation it needs without narrating it. The other holdings she mentions when asked are named as her family's own arrangements, not as steps to take. The existence of the room rate posting reaches the agent only through the published terms of the deposit.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: authorise_reservation_deposit_3e63cb2f in task_tools.py reads the reservation row only to carry its customer and season onto the folio entry and to raise the deposit held; it looks at no folio entry, tests no balance, compares no state and returns no policy refusal, so it writes the deposit faithfully whether or not a room rate stands on the folio. post_stay_room_charge_ee3504ba likewise checks nothing about the deposit. An agent that takes the deposit without pricing the stay gets a receipt, and is wrong only in the terminal records.
